record_scope_reconstruction: Two separate Myawaddy–Mae Sot facilities and traffic restrictions: Bridge II cargo interruption during April 2024 fighting, and Thai admission restrictions on temporary-pass/booklet holders at Bridge I from 21 April. Passport permission and later document-specific access are retained. Inland Asia Highway damage is outside these bridge points.

May 1 UID requirement is later documentation policy, not evidence of the first Thai readmission or April onset.
Named first Moei road bridge geometry inspected; distinct from Mae Sai.

phase_decisions.phase_applicability: Bridge II cargo only. Conflicting April onset dates and April 30 observed truck return retained.

date_scope_check.finding: Geography review only. Current phase bounds, traffic exceptions, uncertain onset, reopening status and >24-hour decision are retained; current map features are not evidence of historical operation.
date_scope_check.qualification:
REC50-R28-001-P1: RFA’s April 30 report describes trucks returning after ten days, and Eleven’s May 1 report explicitly gives April 20. GNLM’s May 8 retrospective gives April 11. Both concern Bridge II cargo, so the onset conflict remains visible; the matched April 30 truck return and sustained interruption support qualified visualization and greater-than-24-hour eligibility. Exact elapsed duration and imposing-side attribution remain unresolved. CNI’s May 5 combined account mentions April 21 for suspended activities at both bridges; it does not resolve the cargo-specific disagreement. Inland Asia Highway damage is separate from passage over the international bridge.

REC50-R28-001-P2: Generic April 27 reopening and travel into Myanmar alone do not establish restored Thai admission for pass holders. May reports now supply document-specific conditional access, bounded by May 6 without claiming the first Thai readmission or restoration of every booklet type. IMNA’s March 1 UID date conflicts with MOI and Eleven’s May 1 account and is not used. The official rationale for the original Thai document refusal remains unknown; later Myanmar UID policy motives are not retroactively assigned to it. February 2026 guarantor conditions are a later observation, not evidence of uninterrupted April 2024–2026 restrictions.
